title: Reservation adjudication and autoscale safeguards playbook
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Purpose: create a deterministic, auditable provisioning workflow for Dedicated reservations that enforces throughput guarantees while protecting fleet health via autoscale safeguards and admission controls. Scope: reservation intake, eligibility checks, approval matrix, billing & commitment staging, autoscale policy templates (min/target/max, burst windows, cooldown), simulation harness for rejection/eviction scenarios, and operator runbooks for escalations.

Key outcomes: Clear decision gates for accepting reservation requests, standard autoscale policy templates tied to workload patterns, tool-assisted capacity simulations to validate SLO commitments before approval, and automated post-approval onboarding steps (quota assignment, model pinning, monitoring links).

Stakeholders: PM (Capacity & Dedicated), Eng (Serving runtime, Autoscale, Infra), Solutions Eng, Billing, Legal (contract terms), Support on-call, Customer Success.

Admission checks (to implement in intake service):
- Org eligibility: contract tier, outstanding invoices, region compatibility.
- Workload fit: steady throughput vs. bursty; token-per-second distribution; KV cache pressure estimate.
- Fleet health check: available headroom on requested GPU family and region within the requested commit window.
- Security/compliance flags: private deployment requirements / VPC constraints.

Approval matrix (decision tree):
- Auto-approve: standard pattern + within capacity & no legal/KYC flags + <$50k ARR-equivalent commit.
- Manual review required: custom network/KMS, >$50k ARR-equivalent, multi-region failover requested, or predicted headroom <15%.
- Exec review: strategic customers requesting >3 month dedicated fleet blocks or non-standard SLAs.

Autoscale safeguard primitives:
- Soft quota (target throughput): encourages autoscaling but preserves minimal reservation.
- Hard floor (min throughput) tied to paid commit to prevent aggressive scale-to-zero.
- Burst credits: allows short windows of >target throughput using a token-bucket; decays over time and observable in console.
- Cooldown windows and decay policies to prevent oscillation, with defaults based on GPU family and model latency profile.
- Preemption policy: clear rules for fallback to pooled capacity or model-variant downgrade if reservation FIFO is saturated.

Simulation & validation:
- Inputs: historical traffic (if customer supplies), synthetic workloads derived from service-level profile, sequence length distribution, and KV cache hit-rate assumptions.
- Outputs: predicted p50/p95 latency, sustained throughput, tail latency under cache-miss heavy conditions, percentage of time autoscale would trigger, and estimated monthly cost.
- Acceptance criteria: predicted p95 latency within committed SLO 95% of simulated windows, predicted monthly cost within +/-15% of quoted bill, and <5% simulated eviction probability under typical failure scenarios.

Operational runbooks (post-approval):
- Onboarding steps: create reservation object, assign quotas, pin model versions, provision monitoring dashboards, enable alerting and SLO tracking, send customer onboarding packet.
- Escalation: if observed fleet headroom drops below 10% for >15 minutes, notify Fleet Ops and trigger temporary burst mitigation (rate-limited thinning) and customer notice.
- Decommissioning: graceful decommit flow with 30-day notice, snapshot KV caches, and rollback plan for pinned models.

Telemetry & dashboards required: reservation-lifecycle dashboard (intake → approval → provisioning → live), commitment utilization heatmap, autoscale event stream, rejection and preemption audit log, cost vs. forecast reconciliation.

Artifacts to produce: intake form schema, autoscale policy templates (three defaults: steady, bursty, mission-critical), approval playbook PDF, simulation harness CLI and link to runbook, dashboard mocks.

Success metrics: time from request → approval (goal <48h for auto-approve), accuracy of simulation vs. first-month usage (target within 20%), reduction in post-provision SLO complaints by 40% for new reservations, and fewer than 2 production evictions per quarter attributable to overcommit mistakes.
